messages:
marta_cs: Heads-up — Greenfield Capital just escalated. They say our API is returning 'meeting minutes' with invented board members and future dates. They claim this started immediately after the auth token caching change rolled today. :warning:

marta_cs: Customer pasted an example in their ticket: ```
Q: Summarize uploaded minutes.
A: Board meeting on 2026-10-12. Attendees: John Harrow (CEO), Elise Mendez (CFO), Pierre Valdez (CTO). Decisions: approve Series C at $120M, hire external auditor 'Northbridge & Co'.
``` They say none of these names or dates exist in their doc.

raj_engineering: Can you paste the raw request headers/route + request_id and which model variant they hit?

marta_cs: Request_id: rq_8f9a2c. Route: POST /v1/chat/completions. Model header: redwood-chat-large-v2. Prompt was simple: "Summarize the attached transcript" with file id ff_44.

alex_support: I pulled the transcript from the ticket (redacted). It contains minutes but none of those names or the 2026 date. Customer says historically outputs matched. They tested yesterday and were fine. :thinking_face:

nina_research: Noting: we rolled auth token caching (service auth-proxy) + faster session reuse at ~11:04 UTC which also flipped a routing optimization that reduces prefix KV caching for attachments. If a KV miss falls through we sometimes route to a lower-capacity variant for faster tail latency. That could change generation behavior.

sasha_sre: Deploy bot shows deploy by raj at 2026-03-15T11:04:52Z. :deploy:

deploy-bot: deploy-complete: service=auth-proxy commit=3f9d1a author=raj status=success time=2026-03-15T11:04:52Z

raj_engineering: Hmm. The auth cache change touched session affinity / model affinity code. If an attachment triggers a cache miss we may have been falling back to redwood-chat-medium-v2 for some requests. Medium has known calibration differences on factuality in long-context summarization.

tom_product: Customer impact is high — they are a payments customer, sensitive to fabricated financial decisions. We need repro steps and immediate mitigation (pin model or rollback).

marta_cs: Customer tried rerunning the same request 3x and got different invented names each time. They attached one more example.

alex_support: Repro attempt from our side: POST same payload -> first hit returned accurate names, second run returned invented attendees. We captured response headers: x-model-served: redwood-chat-medium-v2 for the bad run, x-kv-cache: miss, x-route-fallback: true.

nina_research: That matches hypothesis. Likely sequence: auth-proxy reuse changed routing, cache miss -> fallback path -> medium variant -> different decoding profile -> assertive but hallucinated fillers.

raj_engineering: Short-term mitigation: pin the customer's requests to redwood-chat-large-v2 via routing override (customer token scope) and disable the fallback path for summary routes. I'll push a hotfix to disable fallback within 30m.

marta_cs: I told customer we'll pin them and escalate to eng. They asked for timeline and if rollback is possible.

sasha_sre: Rollback of auth-proxy is possible but has risk to latency/connection storms. Prefer targeted routing override for now.

lucy_privacy: Also flagging compliance — fabricated financial decisions could be sensitive. Keep audit logs and the original transcripts preserved. Notify legal if customer threatens external notice.

tom_product: Action list: 1) raj to disable fallback on summary routes and pin customer -> ETA 30m, 2) nina to run calibration tests to compare factuality metrics between large and medium on their transcript set -> ETA 4h, 3) sasha to monitor error/latency regressions if we rollback -> ETA immediate watch window, 4) marta to update customer in 15m.

raj_engineering: On it. I'll post once override is live and include request_ids to verify served-model header.

marta_cs: Thanks — customer now on a bridge with product and legal. I'll post any new examples here. :eyes:
